questions.q: According to this lesson, what is the single biggest factor in choosing between Terraform and Bicep?
options: Which tool was released more recently
Which tool has a prettier syntax
Whether the project is single-cloud (Azure-only) or multi-cloud
Whether the team prefers JSON over YAML
questions.explain: Bicep only works for Azure; Terraform works across providers with one workflow — that fact drives most of the real decision.

questions.q: What real overhead does Bicep avoid that Terraform requires?
options: Managing a separate state file or backend yourself
Installing a CLI at all
Using a version control system
Writing any parameters or variables
questions.explain: ARM itself tracks what a Bicep deployment created, so there's no separate state file to store, secure, or lock, unlike Terraform's state management.

questions.q: What is a real advantage Terraform has over Bicep, according to this lesson?
options: Zero need to manage state of any kind
A multi-cloud workflow and a much larger module ecosystem via the Terraform Registry
No CLI installation required
First-party, same-day support for new Azure resource types
questions.explain: Terraform manages Azure, AWS, Google Cloud, and more with one CLI, and its Registry's module ecosystem is far larger than Bicep's Azure Verified Modules alone.

questions.q: Why might a team already skilled in Terraform choose to stick with it even for Azure-only work?
options: Terraform has no state management overhead in that scenario
Terraform is required by Microsoft for all Azure deployments
The cost of introducing a second IaC language and toolchain can outweigh Bicep's state-free simplicity
Bicep cannot deploy to Azure at all
questions.explain: Tooling overhead is a real cost — maintaining a second IaC language and CI/CD setup can cost more than the state management Terraform already requires.

questions.q: In the lesson's practical framework, what should you ask first when choosing between the two tools?
options: Is this project Azure-only today, with no realistic multi-cloud need on the horizon?
Does the team prefer HCL or Bicep syntax?
Which tool has more GitHub stars?
Is the project already in production?
questions.explain: The framework starts with clouds needed, not tool preference — if the project is Azure-only with no real multi-cloud need, that leans toward Bicep; otherwise, toward Terraform.
